1.4 **The full source upper chart and simple classes.** The independent construction [[lem-finite-type-a-full-tensor-source-upper-charts-and-string-leading-terms]] applies to every finite cut of the complete minuscule tensor module, in both factor orders. It dualizes the entire reverse lower tensor construction through $H(x,y)=C(\widetilde\psi x,y)$, whose raw monomial Gram matrix is $I$ and whose coefficient conjugation exchanges $A_0(s^{-1})$ with $A_0(s)$. This produces the actual balanced source-upper triple with lifts $L_A$, rather than inferring upper crystal hypotheses from triangularity alone. Its endpoint divided-power argument proves $\ker E_i^{n+1}=\operatorname{span}\{L_A:\varepsilon_i(A)\le n\}$ and the corresponding $F_i$ statement, so the maximal nonzero iteration heights of $L_A$ are precisely $\varepsilon_i(A),\varphi_i(A)$. The KL theorem of [F4] identifies the genuine standard/simple composition matrix with $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(1)L_A$. Since both matrices are unitriangular, their inverses identify the simple class $[L(A)]$ with the actual source vector $L_A$ at $1$. The standard-class translation action of [F1] therefore carries this simple-class identification through every residue iteration. [F6, F1, F4, algebra]

use_locations.text: [F6] Independent tensor coefficient bridge ([[lem-finite-type-a-tensor-hecke-bars-and-complementary-coefficient-charts]]): reciprocal generator action and induced bar, signed positive chart, complementary longest-element spherical inverse chart, and ordinary-bar signed exterior embedding in both factor orders.

4.1 **The independent tensor/wedge bridge and opposite flag.** Apply [[lem-finite-type-a-tensor-hecke-bars-and-complementary-coefficient-charts]] before making any categorical identification. Its tensor generators act at $v=s^{-1}$, its positive chart transports to the sign module by $G_i=-H_i$ at $v=s$, and its complementary representative is $w_Kd(A)w_0$. The proved inverse tensor coefficient is $s^{\ell(w_C)-\ell(w_A)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(s^{-2})$, so its value at $1$ is exactly the ordinary singular composition number in [F3]. The primitive ordinary-bar exterior embedding has coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}$ on column permutations $C$ and sends the wedge $L_A$ to the ambient $L_{a(A)}$. Its signed inverse formula at $1$ therefore agrees term for term with finite Levi Weyl cancellation of the genuine generalized-standard character: $d_{A,B}(1)=[\Delta(B):L(A)]$. This uses character injectivity, and it keeps the equal-entry stabilizer separate from the column Levi. The helper proves the same transport for reversed factors; hence $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]$. At $s=1$ the ordinary tensor bar matrix is the identity (each adjacent exchange has correction $s^{-1}-s=0$), so the reverse form of [F4] has monomial Gram matrix $I$. The identity $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ now says that the monomial coefficient matrix of $T$ is the transpose inverse of the coefficient matrix of $\widetilde L$, namely $\widetilde d^{\mathsf T}$. Thus the coefficient of $M(A)$ in $T_B$ at $1$ is $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]=(X(B):\Delta(A))$ by step 3.1. All sign, longest-element and reverse-factor transports have been proved independently of this linkage conclusion. [F6, F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, algebra]
